# Resume Website Requirements Quality Checklist

**Purpose**: Review the professional resume website requirements for completeness, clarity, consistency, and coverage before implementation begins.
**Created**: 2026-10-07
**Feature**: spec.md

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are the required resume sections for identity, summary, experience, skills, and education explicitly defined for both the standalone resume and the website? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are the rules for optional sections and missing data clearly specified so the site does not invent or imply unavailable experience, education, or portfolio items? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-009, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are working contact and professional-profile requirements defined for all valid owner-supplied links, including the behavior when a link is absent or invalid? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, Gap]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are print and save requirements defined for resume output, including page completeness and exclusion of website-only controls? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, Gap]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 - Is the meaning of "clear, credible professional resume" and "easy-to-scan" quantified in terms of layout, hierarchy, or readability requirements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, Ambiguity]
- [ ] CHK006 - Are "clear, professional language" and "consistent dates and labels" defined with enough specificity to avoid style drift between sections? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is the phrase "primary resume sections discoverable from the main page" explicit enough to define the required placement, prominence, and navigation behavior? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, Ambiguity]
- [ ] CHK008 - Are "readable and operable on common narrow and wide screen sizes" and "without horizontal scrolling" defined with measurable viewport expectations? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, SC-003]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 - Do resume-content requirements remain consistent across the standalone resume, the website, and the print/save output without allowing unsupported claims or conflicting facts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-007, SC-002]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are the rules for optional sections, contact links, and profile details consistent across different content states such as missing education, missing portfolio links, or invalid URLs? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-005, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK011 - Are the requirements for accessibility and responsive readability consistent with the constitutional constraints for WCAG 2.2 AA and static GitHub Pages delivery? [Consistency, Constitution §II, Constitution §III, Spec §FR-006]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK012 - Are the success criteria measurable enough to judge whether the resume is understandable within 30 seconds and whether the layout supports quick scanning? [Acceptance Criteria, SC-001, SC-005]
- [ ] CHK013 - Can the print and responsive success criteria be objectively observed without relying on vague terms like "looks good" or "works properly"? [Measurability, SC-003, SC-004, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK014 - Are the criteria for zero unsupported claims, owner approval, and factual consistency sufficiently objective to support a pre-publication review gate? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-009, SC-002, Assumption]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK015 - Are zero-state and partial-data scenarios defined for missing profile details, limited experience, absent links, and absent optional sections? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK016 - Are exception scenarios defined for broken or invalid contact/profile links, unclear role titles, and long content that must remain legible on narrow screens or in print? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK017 - Are recovery or fallback requirements defined for cases where the resume content cannot be fully validated or optional resources are unavailable? [Coverage, Recovery, Gap, Spec §FR-009]

## Non-Functional Requirements and Dependencies

- [ ] CHK018 - Are accessibility requirements for keyboard access, meaningful structure, visible focus, and readability specified sufficiently for the primary resume and contact journey? [Non-Functional, Constitution §II, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK019 - Are privacy and static-hosting requirements clear enough to prevent secret leakage, tracking, or non-static delivery from being introduced as part of the resume build? [Non-Functional, Constitution §IV, Constitution §III, Gap]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are the dependencies and assumptions about owner approval, GitHub Pages static hosting, and the single-candidate scope explicitly documented and consistent with the project constraints? [Dependencies, Assumption, Constitution §III, Constitution §IV, Spec §FR-009]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline to capture open ambiguities, missing details, or approval needs.
